bib.title: Consistency Models
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 202

read.skipped: Proof appendices A and B skimmed (theory); reference list skimmed for lineage.

question: Can a generative model map noise to data in one step while keeping diffusion's compute-quality trade-off and zero-shot editing?
hypothesis: Enforcing self-consistency along probability-flow ODE trajectories yields good one-step and few-step generators, via distillation or standalone training.
contributions: Consistency models: a network f(x_t,t) mapping any point on a PF ODE trajectory to its origin
Consistency distillation (CD) from a pretrained diffusion model
Consistency training (CT) in isolation, no diffusion model
Zero-shot editing (inpainting, colorization, super-resolution, SDEdit) via multistep sampling
New SOTA one-step FID for distillation on CIFAR-10 (3.55) and ImageNet 64 (6.20)

method.summary: Parameterise f_theta(x,t)=c_skip(t)x+c_out(t)F_theta(x,t) with boundary condition f(x,eps)=x. CD minimises d(f_theta(x_{t_{n+1}}),f_theta-(xhat_{t_n})) where xhat comes from one Heun step of a pretrained EDM score model and theta- is an EMA target network. CT replaces the ODE step with x+t z noise pairs and grows N and mu on a schedule.
method.task: one-step/few-step image generation; zero-shot image editing

models.name: Consistency model (CD/CT)
models.architecture: NCSN++ (CIFAR-10); ADM architectures of Dhariwal & Nichol 2021 (ImageNet 64, LSUN 256); same as EDM with modified skip connections
models.init_from: CD: pretrained EDM weights; CT: random init

other.note: trained in-house; LSUN Bedroom 600k iters, LSUN Cat 300k iters, batch 2048 (reduced from 4096)
LPIPS used in PD curves of Fig 4; Tables report l2 PD

training.objective: CD loss with LPIPS metric, lambda=1, EMA target network; CT loss with LPIPS, schedules N(k), mu(k)
training.steps: CIFAR-10 800k; ImageNet 64 CD 600k, CT 800k; LSUN 256 CD 600k, CT 1000k iterations
training.precision: FP16 mixed precision on ImageNet 64 and LSUN 256; not on CIFAR-10
training.regularisation: EMA decay 0.9999 (CIFAR-10), 0.999943 (ImageNet 64, LSUN); zero EMA for CD on LSUN Bedroom

other.CD N: 18 (CIFAR-10), 40 (ImageNet 64), 40 (LSUN 256), assignment inferred from Table 3 column order
other.LPIPS: images upsampled bilinearly to 224x224 for CIFAR-10 and ImageNet 64; no rescaling for LSUN 256
other.Table 3 column parse: Table 3 text extraction is flattened; per-column N and s1 assignment is partly inferred from column order

inference.decoding: Algorithm 1 multistep consistency sampling; time points found by greedy ternary search optimising FID

eval.protocol: FID/IS/Prec/Rec; number of FID samples, seeds and error bars not stated

evidence.quote: We trained all consistency models with the Rectified Adam optimizer (Liu et al., 2019), with no learning rate decay or warm-up, and no weight decay.

limits: Number of samples for FID, seeds and variance not stated.
Evaluated only on images; unconditional or class-conditional small datasets.
Continuous-time CT needs forward-mode autodiff and EDM initialisation due to variance; left to future work.
Only one-step ODE solvers considered; multistep solvers left as future work.
Time-point selection assumes FID is unimodal in next time point; better strategies left as future work.
GANs (StyleGAN-XL, StyleGAN2-ADA, BigGAN-deep) still beat CT/CD on some datasets (Table 1, 2).

terms.definition: f: (x_t,t) -> x_eps, with f(x_t,t)=f(x_t',t') for points on the same PF ODE trajectory

lineage.note: PF ODE trajectories are what consistency models map to origin

lineage.work: Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion Models (EDM)
lineage.note: Teacher model, parameterisation, Heun solver, T=80, eps=0.002

Factors that affect CD and CT on CIFAR-10; best CD config is LPIPS, Heun, N=18.

figures.caption: Multistep image generation with CD; CD outperforms PD across all datasets and sampling steps.
figures.why: FID vs steps for CD vs PD

code.snippet: x <- f(xhat_T, T); for n=1..N-1: z~N(0,I); xhat_tau_n <- x + sqrt(tau_n^2 - eps^2) z; x <- f(xhat_tau_n, tau_n)
